title: On-demand guest access revocation and exportable compliance snapshot
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers operating in regulated jurisdictions need a way to rapidly revoke transient (guest/contractor) access and produce a single, jurisdiction-scoped evidence bundle that proves which identities were revoked, when, and what residual entitlements existed during a retention window. Current systems produce scattered proofs across SCIM logs, SSO session exports, and per-tenant audit tables which are hard to reconcile for a compliance review.
goal: Implement an on-demand revocation flow for guest/temporary access that: 1) triggers immediate session termination for SSO/SAML sessions where possible, 2) updates SCIM/identity state and propagation to downstream services, and 3) emits a signed, exportable compliance snapshot (tarball) that contains timebound entitlements, revocation events, and retention metadata per jurisdiction.
acceptance_criteria: Operator can mark a user as 'guest:revoke-now' in Console and see session termination events within 30s for supported identity providers.
SCIM user state change is propagated to downstream services (RBAC caches, quota service) within the configured tenant propagation SLA (default 60s).

A compliance snapshot can be requested for a tenant and returns a region-scoped tarball containing: user_export.csv, role_bindings.csv, revocations.log, retention_manifest.json, and signed_manifest.sig.
Snapshot generation respects data residency policy: snapshots for EU tenants are produced and stored only in EU-backed storage and encrypted with the tenant KMS key.
The export includes stable identifiers and hash-redacted email addresses to allow verification without exposing PII when configured.
implementation_notes: Workflow: 1) Console issues 'revoke guest' command to Auth Service; 2) Auth emits SAML/SSO logout (where IdP supports backchannel/logout); 3) Identity service marks ephemeral flag and writes SCIM delta; 4) Eventing layer fans out to RBAC cache invalidation and quota service; 5) Snapshotter composes evidence and stores in region-specific compliance S3 bucket encrypted with tenant KMS.
Use existing event bus (Kafka topic: identity.deltas) and build idempotent workers for instant invalidation and for snapshot assembly.
Signed manifest generation: use tenant signing key stored in KMS to produce manifest.sig so security/compliance teams can verify authenticity.
Retention: snapshot manifest contains retention policy pointer (policy id + expiry datetime) and references to retention lifecycle rules for automated deletion or archival per jurisdiction.
SCIM propagation: implement optimistic retry with exponential backoff and a reconciliation job to ensure eventual consistency for tenants with flaky downstream connectors.

Performance trade-off: immediate full snapshot assembly is expensive for large tenants. We'll support two modes: fast-mode (event list + deltas) and full-mode (materialized CSVs). Fast-mode available by default; full-mode is queued and may take up to 15m for very large exports.
Security: mark snapshot downloads with single-use pre-signed URL, require operator MFA for exporting snapshots, and log all snapshot requests to tenant audit with correlation id.
Metrics: add metrics for 'revoke latency', 'scim-propagation-latency', and 'snapshot-generation-duration' and expose them in Console and to PagerDuty for SLA breaches.
